findings.text: follow-on: the after_suite arm names command '... tests/test_contour_tree_sparse_build.py tests/test_contour_tree_merge.py -ra' but its log_path points at logs/head2-sparse.log, whose own header command runs only test_contour_tree_sparse_build.py and whose summary is '9 passed in 197.49s'; the two-file gate the arm claims is not evidenced by the log it records, and the head merge arm exists only as logs/head2-merge.log (11 passed) with no JSON arm. baseline_suite at line 23 likewise names only the sparse file, so the done_when's base arm of the merge file is recorded in no arm. The measurements are real and green on disk; the receipts point a reader at the wrong log.

follow-on: at 2,000 cells outside_present is True, so brute_force=not outside_present is False at line 232, the level-by-level comparison with _component_count/_tree_count at lines 138-149 is skipped, and the pinned digest is not kept (the guard is 'if cells == 550'); those rows retain only the structural relation at lines 122-135. A build returning the same valid-node and valid-arc counts over a reordered 2,000-cell topology therefore satisfies every assertion, so the done_when's 'reference that is valid on any host ... compared array by array' is met for the 550-cell rows and not for the 2,000-cell rows, which the manifest's own follow_ons concede.

follow-on: the module docstring's rationale sentence reads 'a byte-order digest travels between hosts where the traversal does not', which is the opposite of the change's premise: the whole repair exists because the byte-order digest does NOT travel between hosts while the traversal does. The sentence is false as written and inverts the reason the file was rewritten.

follow-on: _perturb_arc_order selects a second env-var mutation, CONTOUR_TREE_ARC_PERTURB=rewire, where the repository's existing declared-mutation idiom is CONTOUR_TREE_CORRUPT at tests/test_contour_tree_brute_force.py; two selectors for one idea invite a red log that does not say which mutation produced it.

follow-on: no recorded log demonstrates the final head's test_sparse_build_matches_carrier_reference failing under the arc perturbation; the perturbation log on disk, logs/head-fleet-sparse-perturb.log, is at revision f3990dc36 and names the pre-rename test_sparse_build_matches_base_receipt, so the done_when's 'failing when the sparse build's arc order is perturbed' is evidenced on an earlier revision of the file rather than the reviewed head.
